origin.description: Facilitates easy alignment of strings within a character vector. Designed to help implementers of formatters for custom data types.
origin.usage: align(x, width = NULL, align = c("left", "right"), space = " ")

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: The width that each string is padded to. If NULL, the maximum display width of the character vector is used (see get_max_extent()).

arguments.name: align
arguments.text: How should strings be aligned? If align = left then padding appears on the right, and vice versa.

arguments.name: space
arguments.text: What character should be used for the padding?

translation.description: Facilitates easy alignment of strings within a character vector. Designed to help implementers of formatters for custom data types.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A character vector. A string returns one string. A list returns a list. None is a missing string.

arguments.name: width
arguments.text: The width that each string is padded to. If None, the maximum display width of a non-empty vector is used.

arguments.name: align
arguments.text: How should strings be aligned? If align is left then padding appears on the right, and vice versa. A unique prefix works. None means left.

arguments.name: space
arguments.text: The string repeated for each column of padding.

translation.details: The pad count is the display width minus the string's display width, and it is never negative. The space string is repeated as a whole, so space "ab" twice is "abab". A missing string is pasted as the letters NA. A fractional pad count is truncated toward zero.
translation.value: The padded string, or a list of padded strings.
